title: Fair-Share Role Allocator & Cut Matrix for Cycle Staffing
creator: Aisha Mehta
description:
Problem: As Redwood scales, PMs are spending too much time arbitrating tradeoffs between teams during cycle planning. We need a fast, repeatable way to (1) allocate available FTE/effort across initiatives and roles, (2) produce defensible scope-cut recommendations, and (3) surface bottlenecks and skill constraints before commits are made.

This ticket delivers the `Fair-Share Role Allocator` (a lightweight spreadsheet + automation) and an accompanying `Cut Matrix` that combines importance, risk, cross-team dependencies, and estimated effort to generate prioritized scope reductions. The allocator accepts inputs (team roster by role, role cost multiplier, critical-path weight, ramp-time) and outputs per-initiative soft/hard allocation buckets and 3 recommended cut candidates per initiative.

Goals: Reduce PM-Engineered arbitrations by 50% in next cycle; provide a single source of truth for staffing conversations; make mid-cycle scope triage repeatable and auditable. Deliverables: Google Sheet + Apps Script, PRD, one-pager for exec review, runbook for PMs and ENG leaders, and two simulated scenarios run with leadership before rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator spreadsheet accepts team-level inputs and outputs per-role allocation summary
Cut Matrix generates prioritized cut list (top 3) for each initiative with rationale fields populated
Runbook published in Confluence with step-by-step usage and decision rules
Two simulated cycle-planning scenarios completed with PM/ENG/Design leads and notes captured
Stakeholder sign-off from Head of Product and Head of Engineering

risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: HR sync data delays could make allocations stale. Mitigation: manual import and explicit TTL on inputs; record source+timestamp in sheet.
Risk: Managers may game multipliers to protect work. Mitigation: require justification field + audit trail for overrides; PM council to review overrides > 10% of baseline.

notes_for_reviewers: When reviewing, focus on: (a) defensibility of the cut scoring formula, (b) ease-of-use for managers entering inputs, (c) auditability of overrides. Expect two iterations after stakeholder simulations.
